record.original_question: Further develop algorithmic information theory for bi-infinite sequences and, more generally, for constructive cpo's. One possible direction mentioned in the source is to use bi-infinite cellular automata as computational models.

evidence.quote: Further develop algorithmic information theory for bi-infinite sequences and, more generally, for constructive cpo’s. (C. Calude, H. Jürgensen) An idea would be to use bi-infinite cellular automata as computational models. (F. Geurts)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a theory of algorithmic information (Kolmogorov complexity, algorithmic randomness, and related notions) for bi-infinite sequences over a finite alphabet — that is, elements of $\Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$ — and, more generally, for constructive complete partial orders (cpo's). 

Concretely, one is asked to: (i) define suitable notions of program-size / prefix / plain complexity, randomness, and information content for bi-infinite sequences $x \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$ that respect the natural shift and reflection symmetries of the two-sided setting; (ii) extend these definitions to elements of an arbitrary constructive cpo $(D, \sqsubseteq)$ (a cpo equipped with an effective presentation of its basis of compact elements), in such a way that the classical theory on one-sided infinite sequences $\Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ is recovered as a special case; and (iii) establish the standard structural results (invariance theorem, characterizations of randomness via tests/martingales/incompressibility, conservation of information, etc.) in this generalized framework. 

A specific suggested computational model for the bi-infinite case is bi-infinite cellular automata: take the model of computation underlying the complexity definitions to be cellular automata acting on configurations in $\Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$, and develop the resulting algorithmic information theory.
artifact.category_tag: algorithmic information theory for bi-infinite sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably by Calude, Hertling, Jürgensen and Weihrauch) developed algorithmic randomness on full shift spaces of bi-infinite sequences, and later authors studied algorithmic information theory in the context of cellular automata dynamics. However, the broader program of developing algorithmic information theory for arbitrary constructive cpo's remains an open-ended research direction rather than a fully resolved problem.
